summary.text: Michael Durso is a Republican member of the New York State Assembly who has represented District 9 on Long Island since 2021 and is running for re-election on the Republican and Conservative lines.
Before his election he worked as a sanitation supervisor and as a public safety officer at Hofstra University.

paragraphs.text: Michael Durso grew up in Massapequa Park in a family that, according to his official biography, worked in a small restaurant and a supermarket deli; his father rose to become president of RWDSU Local Union 338 and the Long Island Federation of Labor.
He began his career as a sanitation worker, later became a sanitation supervisor, and is a member of CSEA Local 881.
He also worked as a public safety officer at Hofstra University, belonged to Teamsters Local 553, and graduated from a carpentry program at BOCES in Levittown.
Durso was elected to the Assembly on November 3, 2020.
His district covers parts of Nassau and Suffolk counties, including South Farmingdale, Massapequa, Massapequa Park, West Babylon, Babylon and West Islip.
He serves on the Consumer Affairs and Protection, Health, Labor, Racing and Wagering, Science and Technology, and Transportation committees.
Durso lives in Massapequa Park with his wife, Dana, and their two daughters.
